_comment: Issue #1096/#1119/#1128: a plain NORMAL-stance MOVE order (target_enemy null) is a disengage command -- the unit marches off toward the new destination immediately, it does NOT pause while State.FIGHTING. What actually gates the outcome is the unit's own lingering-engagement latch (set by the preceding fight, refreshed only while State.FIGHTING) decaying out while the unit is already marching -- once it does, Unit._resolve_disengage_move_order() decides whether the march resumes or cancels, based on whether the destination is now occupied by a living enemy. Order.Guard.ENGAGED_FRACTION_ABOVE just marks which moves opt into this check at all. Stages a sustained, evenly-matched melee (two 40-soldier Spearmen regiments) so a real engagement is on record: at tick 300, with the player heavily engaged, a plain move order is issued to a point just to the side of the clash. The order is accepted (order_guard shows ENGAGED_FRACTION_ABOVE) and the unit starts marching within a few ticks -- but around tick 332, once the unit's own engagement linger decays, the destination still sits inside the enemy's own footprint (it never moved far), so the order is cancelled outright (current_order drops to null) instead of continuing to march -- the unit falls back into the same fight within a couple of ticks rather than straying toward a destination the enemy still holds.
